Winter Walking

Winter walking in the Tiroler Oberland

An ideal altitude and 130 kilometres of prepared routes for winter hiking make the Tiroler Oberland the perfect place for leisure hikers as well as those with sporting ambitions.

We recommend it because:

  • Spectacular high-valley landscapes: winter trails with panoramic views, e.g. the Adlerblick in the Kaunertal or around the Pfundser Tschey nature reserve
  • The unique glacial landscape of the Pitzal and Kaunertal glaciers
  • Guided Nature Watch tours through the Kaunergrat Nature Park

Moonlight Picnic

Far from the brightly lit cities, in the unspoilt high valley beneath the clear starry sky, you can witness unforgettable celestial events such as nights of shooting stars, meteor showers and new moons.

Travelling sustainably

  • The nearest railway station for travelling to Nauders is Landeck-Zams.
  • From there there are regular bus connections (Postbus) to Nauders - an environmentally friendly and convenient connection for rail travellers.
  • Regular direct buses run from Innsbruck, Munich or Merano to Nauders.
  • A ski bus runs between Nauders and the Bergkastel cable car throughout the day
Further information on mobility in Nauders

More about winter hiking in the Tyrolean Oberland

The Tyrolean Oberland impresses with snow-covered winter landscapes, peaceful hiking trails and impressive mountain panoramas. Regions such as Ried, Prutz and Pfunds offer perfectly groomed trails away from the hustle and bustle, ideal for relaxation and enjoying nature.

Popular routes include the evening tour around the Mutzkopf, the winter hike to Altfinstermünz Castle and the tour to the Adlerblick viewing platform in the Kaunertal winter hike. These trails offer a variety of experiences for families, beginners and experienced hikers.

Highlights include the tranquil valleys, snow-covered forests and views of the impressive Tyrolean mountains. The winter hike to the Adlerblick viewing platform and the "Feichti" wildlife enclosure is particularly beautiful.
